# Audit and preserve an existing interface

Inspect the actual framework, components, styling version and user flow. Establish
the intended mode before edits. Audit-only returns prioritized findings with
observable examples and impact. Preserve mode makes bounded improvements while
retaining real copy/data, routes, IDs, analytics, integrations and behavior.
Overhaul changes only the explicitly selected design or functionality.

Assess hierarchy, text length/wrapping, alignment, spacing, meaningful grouping,
contrast and consistent state feedback. Check keyboard focus, form validation,
loading/empty/error states, narrow screens, overflow and reduced motion. Avoid
performing a font swap, icon replacement, random layout change or animation pass
merely to satisfy a preset's ban list.

Prioritize task-blocking and accessibility defects, then hierarchy and consistency,
then optional polish. Preserve legal links and supplied content; do not invent
policies, cookie requirements, statistics, customers or destinations. Distinguish
missing content from deliberately empty or valid zero states.

Work within the existing stack. Check installed dependencies and project conventions
before using an API. Validate the changed flows with actual interaction and relevant
checks; do not claim browser or visual testing from source inspection alone.
